instruction: How to set up a Crossplane AWS provider with IRSA
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-irsa
spec:
  credentials:
    source: IRSA
    roleARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/CrossplaneIRSA'

instruction: How to set up a Crossplane AWS provider with Upbound Universal Crossplane (UXP)
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: upbound-aws
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: upbound-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds'

instruction: How to install Crossplane with UXP
output: helm repo add upbound-stable https://charts.upbound.io/stable && helm install uxp --namespace upbound-system upbound-stable/universal-crossplane

instruction: How to set up a Crossplane ProviderConfig for Upbound AWS
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: upbound-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds'

instruction: How to create a Crossplane managed resource using Upbound provider
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: my-bucket
spec:
  forProvider:
    region: us-east-1
  providerConfigRef:
    name: default'

How to create a Crossplane Composition with a selector
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: with-selector
  labels:
    provider: aws
    tier: production
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
    kind: XMyApp
  resources:
  - name: my-bucket
    base:
      apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
      kind: Bucket
      spec:
        forProvider:
          region: us-east-1'

instruction: How to select a Crossplane Composition based on labels
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: example.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: MyApp
metadata:
  name: my-app-claim
spec:
  compositionSelector:
    matchLabels:
      provider: aws
      tier: production
  resourceRef:
    apiVersion: example.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
    kind: XMyApp
    name: my-app-claim'

How to create a Crossplane store config for secret publishing
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: gcp.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: StoreConfig
metadata:
  name: gcp-store
spec:
  type: GCP
  defaultScope: crossplane-system
  gcp:
    projectID: my-project'

instruction: How to create a Crossplane store config for AWS secrets
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: StoreConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-store
spec:
  type: AWS
  defaultScope: crossplane-system
  aws:
    region: us-east-1'

instruction: How to use a Crossplane store config in a claim
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: example.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: MyApp
metadata:
  name: my-app-claim
spec:
  region: us-east-1
  publishConnectionDetailsTo:
    name: my-app-secret
    configRef:
      name: aws-store'

instruction: How to create a Crossplane environment config
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: EnvironmentConfig
metadata:
  name: default-env
  annotations:
    crossplane.io/environment-config: default
spec:
  data:
    region: us-east-1
    tags:
      environment: production
      managed-by: crossplane'

How to create a Crossplane usage resource
output:
kubectl apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: Usage
metadata:
  name: my-bucket-usage
spec:
  of:
    apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
    kind: Bucket
    resourceRef:
      name: my-bucket
  by:
    apiVersion: example.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
    kind: MyApp
    resourceRef:
      name: my-app-claim'
